title: sessioned-ensemble-promote-with-hybrid-ab-rollback-playbook
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a session-aware ensemble promotion controller and hybrid A/B rollback playbook. Improves safe promotes for stateful session traffic with explainable rollback replay. No API surface changes for customers.
description: Motivation: Large multi-variant experiments and shadow-to-canary promotions expose a gap when session affinity and small cohorts interact with ensemble routing. This change introduces a 'sessioned ensemble promoter' runtime controller that coordinates rolling promotes for ensemble model groups (heterogeneous variants) while preserving session coherence and providing an automated hybrid A/B rollback playbook when drift or latency regressions are detected. High-level goals: 1) maintain session affinity across promotes so user sessions see consistent model variants during a transition, 2) enable multi-arm A/B promotes where traffic fractions shift smoothly based on telemetry, 3) provide an automated rollback path that can perform sampled replay (dry-run) plus deterministic revert when thresholds hit, 4) be non-invasive to existing API surface and compatible with Dedicated/Private deployments. Design summary: The promoter composes three subcomponents: a session ledger that holds session->variant leases, a fractional orchestrator that applies staged traffic deltas with backpressure and decay windows, and a rollback playbook engine that runs a decision DAG (smoke checks, latency SLO gates, quality regression detectors) to trigger sampled replay or immediate revert. The promoter uses a short-lived in-memory lease (default 5m) with optional persistent snapshotting for long-lived sessions behind stateful routes. It integrates with the console telemetry hooks for per-variant SLOs and with the Optimize recommendations engine to pick safe step sizes. Checklist: - [x] API: add internal controller endpoints for orchestration and diagnostics. No public/customer API changes. - [x] Runtime: implement session ledger and fractional orchestrator. - [x] Safety: add rollback playbook engine and decision traces. - [x] Tests: unit tests for lease logic, integration test for staged traffic shift, e2e smoke with simulated regression. - [x] Docs: operator guide and runbook in repo/docs/rollouts. Implementation notes: Commits are split by logical area: session-lease core, orchestrator state machine, rollback playbook DSL and engine, telemetry adapters, tests and docs. The session ledger uses sharded lease buckets keyed by hashed session id to limit coordination hot spots. The fractional orchestrator monitors both request latencies and token-level cost deltas to apply conservative phasing when cost SLOs trend upward. Rollback playbook: default policy is a two-step action: 1) sample-replay mode where 5% of promoted traffic is routed to the previous stable variant for replay and differential comparison for 10 minutes; 2) if delta on chosen metrics exceeds configured thresholds, trigger immediate revert and create an audit snapshot. Backwards compatibility and rollout: the controller starts in dry-run for 48h in a staging cluster with synthetic traffic and can be toggled per-namespace. The operator guide includes manual holdpoints and an emergency 'cut glass' revert route. Testing summary: Added unit coverage to session lease edge cases, an integration harness simulating session churn and heterogenous variant pools, and a simulator that fuzzes latency/regression signals to validate playbook thresholds. CI: initial lint run flagged formatting on DSL parser; fixed in commit 3. Security review: minimal surface; session ids remain hashed; no sensitive state stored unencrypted. Deployment: feature is behind an operator flag (rollouts.session_ensemble_enable) and defaults to off for Dedicated/private installs. Related work: builds on ENG-1425 (cohort-aware promotes) and ENG-1482 (telemetry-led gates). Linear links and SUP ticket noted for support test matrix. Migration and operator impact: small schema bump to internal controller snapshots (v2) with automatic in-place migration script included. Rollback and audit: every promote and revert emits an audit record suitable for retention in customer audit logs for Private deployments. Merge details: squashed and merged to main after approvals and CI green.

review_comments: Calvin Huang: Nice design. Question: how do we avoid hot-sharding on large numbers of short sessions? Suggest adding randomized lease jitter and bucket affinity.
Aisha Patel: Reply: added lease jitter and increased shard count; also added a fallback to sticky short leases for high-churn routes. See session_ledger.go changes in commit c1a6d8f.
Priya Natarajan: Please add an integration test that simulates a regression in both latency and quality signals simultaneously to ensure playbook prioritizes latency SLOs.
Aisha Patel: Added ensemble_fuzzer simulator and an integration test that injects correlated latency+quality drift.
